name: Central Park
description: Iconic 843-acre urban oasis in Manhattan featuring Bethesda Terrace, Bow Bridge, Wollman Rink, and scenic ramble paths.

name: Statue of Liberty
description: Colossal neoclassical copper sculpture on Liberty Island in New York Harbor, a universal symbol of freedom and American heritage.

name: Empire State Building
description: Historic 102-story Art Deco skyscraper in Midtown Manhattan offering panoramic open-air 360° observatory decks.

name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (The Met)
description: One of the world's premier art institutions, housing over two million works spanning 5,000 years of global human creativity.

name: Times Square
description: The pulsing 'Crossroads of the World' known for illuminated Broadway billboards, neon lights, and vibrant pedestrian plazas.

name: Brooklyn Bridge
description: Magnificent 1883 hybrid cable-stayed suspension bridge connecting Manhattan and Brooklyn with a scenic elevated walkway.

name: The High Line
description: Elevated 1.45-mile public greenway and garden path transformed from a historic industrial railway along Manhattan's West Side.

name: One World Trade Center & 9/11 Memorial
description: Western Hemisphere's tallest building alongside the poignant twin reflecting pools honoring the victims in Lower Manhattan.

name: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA)
description: Foremost museum of modern art showcasing masterpieces including Van Gogh's Starry Night, Warhol, Picasso, and Dalí.

name: Rockefeller Center & Top of the Rock
description: Historic Art Deco complex with the famous ice rink, NBC studios, and multi-tiered observation decks looking towards Central Park.

name: Grand Central Terminal
description: World-renowned Beaux-Arts railroad landmark boasting the iconic astronomical ceiling mural, brass clock, and food concourse.

name: American Museum of Natural History
description: Renowned institution celebrated for immense dinosaur fossil halls, the Rose Center for Earth and Space, and biodiversity displays.

name: Washington Square Park
description: Vibrant Greenwich Village civic heart centered on the historic 1892 marble triumphal arch, live jazz performers, and chess games.

name: Chelsea Market
description: Enclosed food hall and artisan marketplace inside a vintage Nabisco industrial bakery in the Meatpacking District.

name: Katz's Delicatessen
description: Legendary Lower East Side Jewish deli serving piled-high hand-sliced pastrami on rye and corned beef sandwiches since 1888.

name: DUMBO & Brooklyn Bridge Park
description: Cobblestone historic waterfront district providing the iconic framed viewpoint of the Manhattan Bridge and Lower Manhattan skyline.

name: Wall Street & Charging Bull
description: Historic birthplace of American high finance featuring Federal Hall, the New York Stock Exchange, and the bronze Charging Bull.

name: Hollywood Sign
description: World-famous 45-foot monumental letters on Mount Lee overlooking Los Angeles, an indelible symbol of the global entertainment capital.

name: Griffith Observatory
description: Spectacular Art Deco public observatory and planetarium with breathtaking vistas spanning downtown Los Angeles to the Pacific Ocean.

name: Santa Monica Pier
description: Historic 1909 ocean pier marking the western terminus of Route 66, home to Pacific Park's solar-powered Ferris wheel and seaside dining.

name: The Getty Center
description: Richard Meier-designed architectural campus in Brentwood displaying European paintings, sculptures, and travertine courtyard gardens.

name: Hollywood Walk of Fame
description: Famous 15-block sidewalk along Hollywood Boulevard embedded with more than 2,700 brass stars honoring legends of film and music.

name: Venice Beach Boardwalk
description: Vibrant seaside promenade famed for eccentric street performers, Muscle Beach outdoor gym, oceanfront skate park, and street art.

name: LACMA (Urban Light)
description: Major art museum complex in Miracle Mile, internationally celebrated for Chris Burden's 'Urban Light' assemblage of 202 historic lampposts.

name: Golden Gate Bridge
description: Internationally recognized 1.7-mile Art Deco suspension span in International Orange arching majestically across the Golden Gate strait.

name: Alcatraz Island
description: Former federal maximum-security penitentiary on a rocky island in San Francisco Bay that held notorious convicts like Al Capone.

name: Fisherman's Wharf & Pier 39
description: Historic waterfront destination renowned for sunbathing sea lions, freshly steamed clam chowder in sourdough bowls, and bay cruises.

name: Palace of Fine Arts
description: Monumental Greco-Roman rotunda and colonnade originally built for the 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition, mirrored in a tranquil swan lagoon.

name: Lombard Street (Crooked Street)
description: The famously steep 'crookedest street in the world' featuring eight tight hairpin switchbacks paved in red brick and bordered by hydrangeas.

name: Golden Gate Park
description: Sprawling 1,017-acre sanctuary housing the Japanese Tea Garden, Conservatory of Flowers, California Academy of Sciences, and bison paddock.

name: Millennium Park & Cloud Gate (The Bean)
description: Chicago's premier civic gathering space featuring Anish Kapoor's seamless polished stainless steel sculpture reflecting the skyline.

name: Art Institute of Chicago
description: Legendary museum guarding one of the world's finest collections of Impressionist and American masterpieces including Nighthawks.

name: Navy Pier
description: Historic 3,300-foot landmark pier stretching into Lake Michigan, featuring the Centennial Wheel, waterside eateries, and tour boats.

name: Willis Tower Skydeck
description: 103rd-floor skyscraper observation deck with 'The Ledge' — glass-bottomed boxes projecting 4.3 feet out into the open sky.
